name: Portbou – Walter Benjamin memorial 'Passatges'
story: Portbou, the railway frontier town, was one of the main crossing points of the Retirada in February 1939. Eighteen months later the flow ran the other way: refugees from Nazi-occupied France tried to reach Spain and Portugal. On 26 September 1940 the German-Jewish philosopher Walter Benjamin, turned back by the Spanish authorities after crossing the Pyrenees on foot, took his own life here. Dani Karavan's memorial 'Passatges' (1994) is a steel corridor descending towards the sea. It belongs to the story of exile rather than to the Civil War itself.
see: Karavan's steel stairway descending towards the sea beside the cemetery, Benjamin's memorial stone, and the view over the bay.
plan: Free; a short walk up from the station to the cemetery; combine with the border crossing to Cerbère.
